admin.aboveZero: Use a value greater than zero.
admin.areaExplains: An area is where work is filed. Declaring one here is what stops two spellings of the same name becoming two areas that never meet.
admin.areaFolds: Becomes a lowercase identifier, without accents and with hyphens in place of spaces.
admin.areaHint: An area is where work is filed: an agent belongs to one, a ceiling governs one, a policy reaches a set of them and a grant is held in one. Undeclared, every screen invents its own from whatever exists.
admin.assistantEffortHint: How hard it thinks before answering. Organising text into fields does not ask for much; raise it only if the readings come back shallow.
admin.authoringHint: The model that conducts the interview and writes the read-back when an agent is created. It is not the provider agents use to run: this one never touches a customer system, it only produces text a person approves.
admin.ceilingApplies: Applies from the next run; one already stopped resumes when there is room.
admin.ceilingsInherit: Ceilings inherit downwards and never widen: an area cannot raise what its company allows. Reaching one pauses the run and it continues from where it stopped, rather than ending.
admin.companyFixed: A company is created at installation, not here.
admin.connectFirst: The assistant points at a provider already connected under Integrations. Connect one there first — the credential lives in a single place.
admin.effectDestructive: Erases or replaces in a way that is hard to undo.

effectHint.destructive: Deletes or overwrites in a way that is hard to undo.
effectHint.write: Changes something, and it can be reversed.

admin.eventsHint: Every configuration change appears here with who made it and when: classifying a tool, registering a provider, removing a server.
admin.inCurrency: In the installation's currency. Leave empty not to cap by amount.
admin.name: Name
admin.noCeilingHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is what each agent specification sets per run — nobody can cap an area. Reaching a ceiling pauses the run and it continues later.
admin.noPricesHint: With no rate every cost in the console reads zero: the platform counts tokens and refuses to guess at money. Run ceilings, area ceilings and the authoring assistant's bound are all without effect.
admin.rateApplies: Applies to runs started after the workers reload. What is already in the ledger keeps the money it was recorded with.
admin.rateLine: in {{input}} · out {{output}} · cache read {{cacheRead}} · cache write {{cacheWrite}}
admin.ratesAreYours: Nothing arrives filled in: rates vary by contract, and a wrong one is worse than none — it is a number somebody trusts.
admin.readMarksRun: A read marks the run. A write after that stops for a person to decide.
admin.reasonPlaceholder: records an internal note on the CRM
admin.recordedInTrail: Recorded in your name in the administrative trail. Correcting it later creates a new record; no record is erased.
admin.removeCeiling: Runs in that scope become bounded only by each agent's per-run ceiling. It is recorded in the trail.
admin.removeRateHint: Runs on this model go back to being recorded in tokens, without money. What is already in the ledger does not change.
admin.sayCompany: Say which company the area belongs to.
admin.sayScope: Say what this ceiling applies to.
admin.subtitle: What the platform talks to, what each tool does to the world, and who changed what.
admin.toolsEmptyHint: Tools appear here when a worker connects to an MCP server configured below and publishes what it found.
admin.undoTakesTheResult: The undo is called with what this tool returned. Leave it empty if an act by this tool cannot be taken back by machine — abandoning a run will say so rather than hide it.
admin.whatItDoes: What this tool does to the world
admin.withdrawArea: It stops being offered for new work. The agents, ceilings and policies already filed under it keep pointing at it and keep applying — withdrawing an area and rewriting the past are different acts.
admin.arriveUnclassified: tools arrive unclassified and are refused until ruled
admin.waitingForARuling_one: {{count}} tool is refused until somebody rules on it
admin.waitingForARuling_other: {{count}} tools are refused until somebody rules on them
admin.nothingWaitingHint: Every tool this installation brought in has been ruled on. New ones appear here when a server offers them, and when one changes under a ruling somebody made.

agents.callerAlsoNeeds: The caller also has to send an
agents.catalogueIsTheOrgs: The catalogue is the organisation's. Here you choose what this agent may invoke.

agents.deniesWhatTheTextPromises: already denies what the text promises:

agents.emptyHint: Agents appear here when a worker publishes the definitions it loaded. Each publication creates a new version; the previous one stays readable.
agents.flowClean: No data from outside reaches a tool that acts on the world.
agents.flowHint: Click a card to edit it beside. The order is changed in Text.
agents.flowPath: {{from}} brings data from outside and {{to}} acts on it

agents.hintGovernance: Who fires it, how far it goes, and the reading you approve.
agents.hintSteps: The same sequence, as text or as a flow — your choice.
agents.hintTools: The catalogue is the organisation's; this is what this agent may invoke.

agents.instructionsHint: What the model receives, word for word.

agents.ladderAlreadyDenies: The platform already denies it, by effect:
agents.ladderDeniesInStrip: The platform already denies it, by effect:
agents.manualOnly: No trigger. This agent only runs when somebody presses the button.
agents.noEventsHint: An agent that declares emits publishes the event when one of its runs finishes, and another that declares an event trigger starts from it. Neither names the other.
agents.noMatch: No agent with that name, in that area and in that state.
agents.noStepsMeans: No steps declared: the run has one envelope, holding the whole pack from start to finish.
agents.noTools: No tool. This agent cannot touch anything outside the model.
agents.noTriggers: Nothing. This agent only runs when somebody opens it here.
agents.notEnabledInStrip: is not enabled on this agent:
agents.notHereNotInvokable: What is not here cannot be invoked, whatever the instructions ask for.
agents.notInThePack: The pack a run is offered is what the agent has enabled. A tool outside it cannot even be proposed by the model: the sentence describes a step that does not happen, and the trail afterwards does not say why.
agents.notInThePackYet: not in this agent's pack yet
agents.nothingChanged: Nothing changed. Publishing now would return the version that already exists: the version is the digest of the content, and the same text is the same version.
agents.nothingToGate: Nothing for the Gate to decide: this stage calls no tool.
agents.packEmptyForStep: The agent has no tools in its pack yet.
agents.pausedOnCreate: A new agent is created paused. Publishing writes the definition; starting is a separate decision, and all four ways of opening a run obey it.
agents.pausedStartWhenReady: The agent is paused. Start it when you want it to run.
agents.payloadIsThis: This is exactly what leaves for the model. Labels become plain lines; nothing is added.
agents.pickAStep: Pick a card to edit, or drag something from the pack in.
agents.proseUnchanged: The prose has not changed since the published version.
agents.publishWritesVersion: Publishing writes a new version. Runs already made stay pinned to the version that ran in them.
agents.publishedWithout: This version was published with no instructions.
agents.reachesNothing: reaches no tool — the agent thinking
agents.readAgainExplains: This replaces the {{count}} drawn steps with a fresh reading of the text. If the text has not changed, you get back the reading you already had — and lose what you arranged by hand.
agents.readTheInstructions: Read the instructions and propose the steps
agents.readingNow: Reading the instructions and laying out the stages…
agents.retireExplains: It leaves the lists and stops running. Nothing is deleted: the versions and the runs stay readable, because a run is only explained by the version it ran under. You can bring it back later.
agents.rightColumnIsPolicy: The right-hand column is what the policy in force will do, not a setting on this agent. Changing it means editing the policy — which has an owner, a reason and a code that appears in the trail.
agents.riskFromOutside_one: 1 brings data from outside, which marks the run.
agents.riskFromOutside_other: {{count}} bring data from outside, which marks the run.
agents.riskNothing: Nothing. With no tools, this agent can only reason.
agents.riskUnclassified_one: 1 unclassified — it will not run until the Curator rules on it.
agents.riskUnclassified_other: {{count}} unclassified — they will not run until the Curator rules on them.
agents.rotateWarning: The current key stops working immediately. Every system configured with it will start receiving 401 until it is updated with the new one.
agents.runOpensOnPublished: The run opens on the version published now and is recorded in your name. A person still decides any action that requires approval.
agents.runsStayPinned: Runs in flight stay pinned to the version they started on.
agents.runsUnreadable: Could not read this agent's runs.
agents.sameThing: Text and flow are the same thing seen two ways: what you change in one shows in the other.
agents.searchTools: Search a tool, or what it does
agents.startFromHint: Four recurring cases. You adjust the text and choose the tools below — a template brings none, because which ones exist here is the Curator's decision.
agents.stepsHint: A reading of the instructions, in stages. The instructions stay the text; this is what the Gate should obey at each moment.
agents.stepsProposedHint: Check and correct them: what stays here is what counts. Tools outside the pack were dropped.
agents.subtitle: Every published version is immutable: the identifier is the digest of the content, so the text a run executed can always be read back.
agents.textAlreadyPublished: This text was already the published version.
agents.textHint: Write the sequence as sentences. Drag by the grip to reorder.
agents.triggerChannelExplains: Starts when somebody mentions the agent in a conversation of its own area. Which conversations those are is decided in Integrations.

triggerNeeds.cron: With no expression this trigger never fires.
triggerNeeds.webhook: With no path this trigger never fires.
triggerNeeds.event: With no event name this trigger never fires.

agents.triggersHint: What starts a run without anybody asking. It grants nothing: what the agent may do is still the pack and the policies.
agents.undescribed_one: The instructions never mention {{tools}}, which a step may call. The agent is allowed something nobody wrote down.
agents.undescribed_other: The instructions never mention {{tools}}, which the steps may call. The agent is allowed something nobody wrote down.
agents.waitingAndLastRun: {{count}} waiting on a person · last run {{when}}
agents.writeFirst: Write the instructions first. The stages are a reading of them — with no text there is nothing to read.
agents.zeroIsNoCeiling: Zero means no ceiling, which is not the same as a ceiling of zero.

approvals.emptyHint: When an agent proposes an action that needs a human decision, it appears here with the reason and what the action does.
approvals.notePlaceholder: Stays in the trail alongside the decision
approvals.subtitle: Steps where an agent stopped because a person has to decide. The decision stays in the trail, with whoever made it.
approvals.willRunNamed: The tool {{tool}} will run, and the effect will be recorded on the trail in your name.

audit.emptyHint: The Gate's decisions, the human approvals and every change anybody makes to the rules appear here — classifying a tool, configuring a provider, setting a ceiling.
audit.sealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> ledger entries, chained by hash — each one seals the one before it.
audit.subtitle: What the agents did and what people changed in the rules they run under. Both records are append-only; only one is chained.
audit.unsealedEntries: <n>{{count}}</n> from the administrative trail: append-only by grant, not chained.
audit.verifyIsPerRun: Verifying the chain is done per run, in that run's trail.

common.loadFailedHint: Check the connection to the server and try again.

compensation.abandonHint: A parked run is paused, not over: raising a ceiling continues it from where it stopped. Ending it says it will not continue.
compensation.abandonedAsIs: The world was left as it was. Nothing was undone.
compensation.abandonedUndoing: A worker is undoing what it left. Each step lands on the trail.
compensation.failed: The run could not be ended.
compensation.nothingStanding: This run left nothing to undo.
compensation.undoItHint: Every undo crosses the Gate and is recorded. Turning this off ends the run and leaves the world as it is — sometimes that is right, and it is recorded as the choice it was.
compensation.whyPlaceholder: duplicate charge, the customer was already helped by phone

correction.explains: Tick what should have been true. What you tick is checked on every future version — which is why it is a choice and not free text.
correction.noteHint: For whoever reads it in a year. It is not what the battery checks.
correction.recordedHint: This case joins the battery from now on.

cost.alertApproaching: {{where}} has passed {{threshold}}% of this month's budget
cost.cacheShare: of what went into the model, at a fraction of the price

cost.noCapsHint: With no scope ceiling, the only limit is each agent's own per run. Configure one under Administration → Ceilings.
cost.noTokens: No token accounted for in the period.
cost.spentPerDay: Spent per day over the last 14 days
cost.subtitle: Every run has a known cost before anybody decides to scale it. The run is the accounting unit; agent, area and period are cuts of it.

gate.badArgs: The arguments do not match the tool's contract.

identity.groupsClaimHint: Keycloak and Okta commonly use groups; Entra ID uses roles.

identity.noMapping: No mapping — anyone signing in here receives no access at all.
identity.removeDescription: It stops accepting sign-ins immediately. Sessions already open are unaffected — revoking those is a separate act.
identity.saveFailed: Saved, but not accepting sign-ins yet

integrations.clientKnowsIt: the client already knows the address
integrations.commandRuns: Run by the worker, with the arguments below.

integrations.credentialVault: Sealed in the vault; not even this screen can read it back.
integrations.mcpExplains: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Everything it offers arrives unclassified and is refused until somebody says what it does.
integrations.neverTried: No worker has tried to connect yet.
integrations.noProviderHint: With no provider no run advances: the agent has nothing to plan with.
integrations.noServerHint: An MCP server is what gives agents their tools. Until there is one, agents can only reason.
integrations.referencedBySpecs: It is what agent definitions reference.
integrations.removeProvider: Runs that depend on this provider stop advancing. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.removeServer: Agents lose this server's tools at the next worker restart. It is recorded in the trail.
integrations.serverFromFlag: configured outside the console, by flag or environment
integrations.subtitle: Everything the agents reach outside this installation, and whether it is answering.
integrations.tokenHint: Sent as a Bearer header on every request. Held in the vault.
integrations.tokenKept: Leave blank to keep the stored token.
integrations.toolsAppearHint: The tools appear within half a minute, on a worker's next pass.
integrations.transportHint: A local process is code executed inside the worker's container. A remote address is a request — a far smaller thing to hand somebody.
integrations.acceptLocalExecution: This server runs code inside the worker
integrations.acceptLocalExecutionWhy: A local server is a program this installation starts. It runs as the worker, on its filesystem, and reaches whatever the worker reaches — the Gate decides what a tool may do, and decides nothing about what a process may read. Your name is recorded against this.
integrations.acceptLocalExecutionRequired: Accept what a local server is, or reach this one over HTTP instead.

interview.closingHint: The sign that the work has finished.

interview.howDoYouKnowItIsDone: How do you know you are done?

interview.whatWouldYouNotDecide: What would you not decide on your own?
interview.whenHint: A time of day, an email arriving, a ticket opened.

narrative.asks: It stops and waits for a person before {{tools}}.
narrative.asksNobody: It stops for nobody: everything it does, it does on its own.

narrative.boundedCost: It pauses at {{micros}}, and resumes where it stopped.
narrative.boundedSteps: It pauses at {{steps}} steps, and resumes where it stopped.

people.emptyHint: People appear here after they sign in for the first time through an identity provider.
people.grantedHere: Granted here, directly. It survives the next sign-in.
people.holdsNothing: They cannot do anything yet: grant the roles on this screen.
people.localExplains: An account that signs in with a password, for when no identity provider is configured yet.
people.passwordFloor: A password needs at least 12 characters.

people.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore.
people.usernameShape: Use 3 or more characters: letters, digits, dot, hyphen or underscore.

policies.allMustHold: All of them have to hold.
policies.codeAppears: The code appears in the trail and in the message shown to whoever is denied.
policies.editorSubtitle: A rule evaluated at every agent step: scope, condition, and what happens when it matches.
policies.emptyHint: With no rules written, the built-in default applies: a read passes, a write asks for human approval, and a destructive or financial effect is denied. A written policy tightens that default — or opens an exception with somebody's name on it.
policies.enforcingNextStep: Enforcing from the next agent step.
policies.monitorMode: In monitor mode: evaluated, recorded, changing nothing.
policies.mostRestrictiveWins: The order between policies does not change the outcome: the Gate returns the most restrictive decision among all that match. Deny beats escalate, which beats allow.
policies.noCondition: With no condition the rule covers everything its scope reaches.
policies.noneSelectedCoversAll: None selected covers all of them.
policies.nothingToSimulate: No decision recorded in the period, so there is nothing to simulate. That does not say the rule is harmless — it says there was nothing to compare against.
policies.onlyExceptionIsAllow: The only exception is an allow that matched: it is the one thing that loosens the built-in default, and that is what an exception is.
policies.reasonExplains: It appears in the trail and to whoever is stopped. It is the difference between “blocked by {{code}}” and knowing what to do about it.
policies.reasonPlaceholder: replies to customers go out through a reviewed channel
policies.ruleEvaluated: The rule that will be evaluated
policies.scopeReach: What the rule reaches before any condition.
policies.simulationExplains: Runs this rule against decisions already recorded and shows what it would have done, before saving.
policies.subtitle: The rules the Gate evaluates at every agent step. A policy in monitor mode is evaluated, recorded, and changes nothing.
policies.unknownDecisions: <n>{{count}}</n> decisions could not be answered: this rule reads arguments, and refused calls never stored any. The number above is a floor, not a total.
policies.willApplyAfterReload: It applies at the next agent step once the workers reload the set.
policies.willBeMonitored: It will be evaluated at every step its scope covers, recorded in the trail, and will change no decision.

retention.eraseExplains: What the runs carried goes. The runs and their trail remain — we do not erase the record that something happened, only the personal data inside it.

retention.runsHint: {{count}} named. Find them in the audit trail.
retention.savedHint: It takes effect on the next sweep, which runs once a day.
retention.shorteningWarns: Shortening it erases on the next sweep, and there is no way back. The floor is one day.

runs.ceilingHit: the cost ceiling was reached; raising the limit resumes from here
runs.changedState: This run changed state in at least one system.
runs.contentGone: The content is no longer available. Retention erases it; the trail keeps its digest.

companies.explains: The identifier is fixed; the name is not. Registering grants you inside it, in the same act.
companies.idNeverChanges: Lowercase, digits and hyphens. It reaches URLs and every scope — it does not change.
companies.idShape: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only
companies.noneHint: Register one to separate operations that share neither policy nor budget.

mcp.subtitle: What this server offers, what we brought in, and what each tool may do.
mcp.surfaceIs: Of what this server offers, these are the tools this installation took. Outside the surface a tool is not restricted — it is not here: no agent is told about it and no call reaches it. Bringing one in does not say what it does; that stays the Curator's separate ruling.
mcp.noToolsYet: No tools yet. They appear once a worker has reached this server.
mcp.noSuchServer: No server by that name is configured.
mcp.leavingAffects_one: Leaving this out stops {{agents}}, which still names it.
mcp.leavingAffects_other: Leaving this out stops {{count}} agents that still name it: {{agents}}.
mcp.recipesAre: What this platform has read about servers other people publish. Choosing one fills the form below — none of them is hosted, supported or endorsed here.
mcp.variablesHint: One NAME=value per line. Given to this server's process and to nothing else — it no longer inherits anything from the worker. Kept in the vault, like a token, because the reason a server needs a variable is usually that the variable is a key.
mcp.startFromARecipe: Start from something we know about
mcp.suggests: This platform would call it {{effect}} — open it to see why.
mcp.connectDescription: What it offers arrives unclassified and refused until somebody says what it does.
mcp.catalogueDescription: What this installation reaches, and what it knows how to reach. Connecting one discovers its tools; every one arrives unclassified and refused until somebody says what it does.
mcp.railCaveat: None of these is written, hosted or supported here. What this platform ships is what it has read about them — a recipe fills a form and decides nothing.
mcp.nothingHereHint: Try the whole catalogue, or connect a server by address — this platform does not have to know about it first.
